name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text:
Standardize a single churn log format across all Whisper batches—creative, executive, and tumbling. Production and analytics teams will align on one schema: timestamp, batch type, segment duration, churn count, and error flags. This kills duplicate parsing work and lets us compare churn trends across workflows.

Trade-off: we freeze one schema now, so later tweaks may need schema migrations.

name: Scriv
text: Reel’s churn log risks *metric drift*: a single schema can’t capture the causal misalignment between tumbling windows and sliding windows—churn counts will still mix apples and oranges. Instead, enforce *two* logs: one for tumbling (batch-start aligned) and one for sliding (real-time aligned), with a clear flag in each row. Analytics owns the schema; Production owns the enforcement tool.

name: Chisel
text:
Adopt Reel’s single churn log schema now—timestamp, batch type, segment duration, churn count, and error flags—enforced across all teams. This ends the current chaos where tumbling and sliding batches log churn differently, letting analytics compare trends without extra parsing. The trade-off is accepting some metric drift between window types, but the clarity and speed of a unified view outweighs perfect precision. Production owns the schema; analytics validates it.

name: Sift
text: Chisel’s single schema hides the *metric skew* risk: a churn spike at 4:59.999 still gets logged twice—once in the tumbling batch starting at 5:00, once in the sliding window ending at 5:00. The fix isn’t one log; it’s *time-aligned windows* with a shared key (e.g., "window_start") so analytics can merge them cleanly. Engineering owns the windowing logic; analytics owns the merge rules. Ship the merge spec first, then enforce logs.

name: Scope
text: Adopt Reel’s single churn log schema now—timestamp, batch type, segment duration, churn count, and error flags—enforced across all teams. This ends the current chaos where tumbling and sliding batches log churn differently, letting analytics compare trends without extra parsing. The trade-off is accepting that some edge cases (like 4:59.999 spikes) will still require manual review, but the clarity gained outweighs the risk. Data owns implementation and rollout.

name: Scriv
text: The single-schema push ignores the core problem: tumbling and sliding windows *measure different things*. A shared timestamp won’t fix the double-counting at window edges—it just hides it. The real fix is a dual-log system with a shared key (e.g., "window_start") so analytics can trace churn to its true source. Settle it with a test: run both logs for a week, then compare churn counts at window boundaries—if they diverge, the dual-log wins.
